verdicts.evidence: The encoder/classifier path was implemented in lerd_eeg/, but the logbook explicitly states the dLIF and ERG prior modules were 'specified but not yet coded'; only a transcription/internal-consistency check was performed, not an implementation of the full architecture.

thm41_audit.py computed the event-prior KL two independent ways (direct integral vs change-of-variables Eq 9) across three test configurations, matching to abs diff ≤1e-13; normalization Z_S=1−e^{−R(S)}, KL≥0, S→∞ convergence, and load-bearing hypotheses were all checked with concrete controls.

On the synthetic toy benchmark, the logbook reproduced baseline IoU≈0 at CS≈0.99 and latent-rate estimates within 2–3.4% of LERD's reported medians, but explicitly states LERD's own IoU magnitudes (0.202–0.473) 'were not regenerated' because they require the trained model.
Only a CPU smoke test was run (1 fold, 3/30 epochs, 63% accuracy); the full 5-fold × 30-epoch experiment was not completed, with the logbook citing ~19 h CPU infeasibility and no GPU run performed.
Cohort B (Sadegh-Zadeh et al.) has Data Availability 'Not applicable' and no public mirror was found; no experiments were run on this dataset.

The ablation results (Table 3) were not reproduced at all (requires full model training); the dLIF-inferred frequencies (Figure 2) were not regenerated; only the raw-EEG spectral-slowing biomarker signature was checked on Cohort A (AD centroid below HC in 19/19 channels), which is a proxy for the model-derived claim.

overall: The logbook provides a solid numerical audit of Theorem 4.1's KL identity (verified to machine precision) and partial reproduction of the toy benchmark's baseline-failure and rate-recovery aspects, but does not reproduce any of LERD's trained-model results (IoU magnitudes, classification accuracy, ablation contributions, or dLIF-inferred frequencies) due to compute and data-availability constraints.
